member.summary: Removes statistical outliers from a sequence of long integers using the interquartile range (IQR) method.
member.param: The sequence of long integers to process.
The multiplier for the IQR to determine outlier boundaries. Default is 1.5 (mild outliers).
Optional action to output diagnostic information during calculation.
member.returns: A sequence with outliers removed.

remarks.para: The method uses the following algorithm:

item.description: Sorts data in ascending order
Calculates quartiles (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4)
Computes the interquartile range: IQ = Q3 - Q1
Determines outlier boundaries: Q1 - (IQ × factor) and Q3 + (IQ × factor)
Removes values outside these boundaries

member.name: T:Fuxion.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.HostnameAttribute
member.summary: Validates that a string value is a valid hostname according to RFC 1123.

remarks.para: This attribute validates hostnames using a regular expression that enforces RFC 1123 naming conventions:

item.description: Can contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) and hyphens (-)
Must start and end with an alphanumeric character (not a hyphen)
Each label (segment between dots) can be 1 to 63 characters long
Labels can be separated by dots (.) to form a fully qualified domain name
Cannot start or end with a hyphen

remarks.para: Valid hostnames include simple hostnames (e.g., "server1") and fully qualified domain names (e.g., "www.example.com").

member.name: M:Fuxion.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.HostnameAttribute.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks:
The validation uses the RFC 1123 hostname pattern:
^([a-zA-Z0-9]|[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])(\.([a-zA-Z0-9]|[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9]))*$
This pattern ensures each label starts and ends with an alphanumeric character and can contain hyphens in between.

member.name: T:Fuxion.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.IpAddressAttribute
member.summary: Validates that a string value is a valid IPv4 address.

remarks.para: This attribute validates IPv4 addresses using a regular expression that ensures each octet (segment) is a valid number between 0 and 255.
The validation enforces that:

item.description: The address consists of exactly 4 octets separated by dots (.)
Each octet is a number between 0 and 255
Leading zeros are allowed (e.g., "192.001.002.003" is valid)
No spaces or other characters are allowed

remarks.para: Note: This validator only supports IPv4 addresses. IPv6 addresses are not supported.

member.name: M:Fuxion.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.IpAddressAttribute.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks:
The validation uses a regular expression that matches IPv4 addresses:
^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])$
Each octet can be:
[0-9]: Single digit (0-9)
[1-9][0-9]: Two digits (10-99)
1[0-9]{2}: Three digits starting with 1 (100-199)
2[0-4][0-9]: Three digits starting with 2 and second digit 0-4 (200-249)
25[0-5]: Three digits starting with 25 and last digit 0-5 (250-255)

member.name: T:Fuxion.FunctionalExtensions
member.summary: Provides functional programming extensions for C# objects, including side-effect operations (Tap) and transformation operations (Map) that enable fluent, pipeline-style code similar to F# or LINQ.
member.remarks:
These extensions follow established functional programming patterns:
Tap: Executes a side-effect and returns the original value unchanged (like Ruby's tap, RxJS's tap)
Map: Transforms a value into a new value (like LINQ's Select, but for individual objects)
Do: Executes a side-effect on each element of a collection (lazy evaluation)
ForEach: Executes a side-effect on each element of a collection (eager evaluation)
Naming Convention: Methods with async actions/functions have the Async suffix for consistency and clarity (e.g., ThenTapAsync, ThenMapAsync, DoAsync).

member.name: M:Fuxion.FunctionalExtensions.<G>$8048A6C8BE30A622530249B904B537EB`1.Tap(System.Action{`0})
member.summary: Executes an action on the object and returns it unchanged (fluent API).
member.param: The action to execute on the object.
member.returns: The original object, unchanged.

remarks.para: This method is commonly known as "tap" in functional programming. It allows you to perform side-effects (like logging, debugging, or initialization) without breaking the fluent API flow.
The name "tap" comes from the idea of "tapping into" a pipeline to observe or modify state without changing the flow of data through the pipeline.

member.name: M:Fuxion.FunctionalExtensions.<G>$8048A6C8BE30A622530249B904B537EB`1.Map``1(System.Func{`0,``0})
member.summary: Applies a transformation function to the value and returns the result.
member.typeparam: The type of the result.
member.param: The transformation function.
member.returns: The transformed value.

remarks.para: This method is similar to LINQ's Select, but for individual objects instead of collections. It enables functional programming-style pipelines in C#, similar to F#'s pipe operator (|>).
While this is technically just a wrapper around calling the function directly, it enables a more readable, linear flow of transformations instead of nested function calls.

member.summary: Executes a synchronous action on each element of the sequence as it is enumerated, and yields the elements unchanged.
member.param: The synchronous action to execute on each element.
member.returns: A sequence that yields each element after executing the action on it. The enumeration is lazy - the action is only executed when elements are actually enumerated.

remarks.para: This method maintains lazy evaluation, similar to LINQ's Select or Where. The action is executed element-by-element as the sequence is consumed, not all at once.
This is useful for logging, debugging, or performing side-effects in LINQ pipelines without breaking the lazy evaluation chain.

list.item: ForEach (List only): Executes immediately, returns void
Do (this method): Executes lazily, returns IEnumerable for chaining
Tap: For single objects, not collections

member.summary: Executes a synchronous action on each element of a result immediately (eager evaluation). Returns the original list after all actions have been executed.
member.param: The synchronous action to execute on each element.
Cancellation token.
member.returns: A task that completes with the original list after executing the action on all elements. This is an eager operation - all actions execute immediately after awaiting.

remarks.para:
This is specifically designed for Entity Framework Core scenarios where you need to:
Modify tracked entities immediately
Ensure all side-effects complete before SaveChanges
Maintain the same List reference for tracking

list.item: ThenForEach: Eager (List), immediate execution, same reference

example.code:
// EF Core change tracking - immediate execution var contracts = await db.Contratos .Where(c => c.IdCliente == clientId) .ToListAsync(ct) .ThenForEach(c => c.IdClientePago = newPaymentId, ct) .ConfigureAwait(false);
await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct); // ✅ Changes are tracked immediately

member.name: T:Fuxion.PathStaticExtensions
member.summary: Provides extension methods for path manipulation and comparison using the Fuxion fluent API pattern.

remarks.para: This static class contains extension methods that enable fluent-style path operations through the .Fx.Path syntax. The extensions provide:

item.description: Path comparison: Check if a path is a subpath of another with OS-aware case sensitivity
Path combination: Fluent path concatenation using the / operator with automatic separator normalization
Separator normalization: Automatic handling of mixed path separators ('/' and '\')
OS-aware behavior: Automatic case-sensitive/insensitive comparison based on the operating system

remarks.para: The extensions use the Fuxion extension pattern: path.Fx.Path.Operation() where:

item.description: .Fx - Entry point to Fuxion extensions (from )
.Path - Accesses the path operations wrapper
.Operation() - Performs path operations like

remarks.para: The path operations automatically adapt to the underlying operating system:

item.description: Windows: Case-insensitive comparisons by default, supports both '\' and '/' separators
Unix/Linux: Case-sensitive comparisons by default, uses '/' as the standard separator
macOS: Case-insensitive by default (configurable at filesystem level), uses '/' separator

The method is marked with for optimal performance, as it's a simple wrapper creation that's called frequently in path operations.

member.name: M:Fuxion.PathStaticExtensions.<G>$B6FE03A10A670177CE54FA599F991E7B.IsSubPathOf(System.String,System.Nullable{System.StringComparison})
member.summary: Determines whether the underlying path is a sub-path of the specified base directory path. The comparison normalizes path separators ('/' and '\'). Only matches if the base directory folder name is matched exactly.
member.param: The base directory path to compare against.
The string comparison type to use. When null, defaults to on Windows and on Unix-based systems (case-sensitive file systems).

remarks.para: This method performs several normalization steps to ensure accurate path comparison:

item.description: Null/whitespace check: Returns false if either path is null, empty, or whitespace
OS detection: Determines the default comparison type based on .IsWindows (.NET 5+) or (.NET Standard/Framework)
Separator normalization: Replaces both '\' and '/' with
Trailing separator: Ensures both paths end with a directory separator to prevent partial folder name matches
String comparison: Uses with the determined comparison type

remarks.para: The method ensures trailing separators on both paths to prevent false positives from partial folder name matches. For example, "c:\foobar\file.txt" will NOT match "c:\foo" because "c:\foobar\" does not start with "c:\foo\".

item.description: Windows: Uses (case-insensitive) because NTFS/FAT32 are case-insensitive
Linux/Unix: Uses (case-sensitive) because ext4/XFS are case-sensitive
macOS: Uses by default, though HFS+/APFS can be configured for case-insensitivity

remarks.para: The method normalizes both forward slashes ('/') and backslashes ('\') to the system's native , allowing cross-platform path strings to be compared correctly.

member.name: M:Fuxion.PathStaticExtensions.<G>$B6FE03A10A670177CE54FA599F991E7B.GetDefaultPathComparison
member.summary: Gets the default string comparison type for path operations based on the current operating system. Returns on Windows (case-insensitive file system) and on Unix-based systems (case-sensitive file systems).

remarks.para: This method uses conditional compilation to provide optimal OS detection based on the target framework:

item.description: .NET 5+: Uses .IsWindows for efficient, inline OS detection
.NET Standard 2.0/.NET Framework: Uses with
Windows (NTFS, FAT32): Returns because Windows filesystems are case-insensitive (though they preserve case)
Linux (ext4, XFS, btrfs): Returns because Linux filesystems are case-sensitive
macOS (APFS, HFS+): Returns by default, though APFS can be formatted as case-insensitive

remarks.para: Design note: This method is private because it's an implementation detail of path comparison. External callers should use the comparisonType parameter in if they need to override the default behavior.

member.name: T:Fuxion.Reflection.ReflectionExtensions
member.summary: Provides extension methods for reflection operations on types, members, methods, and assemblies. Includes functionality for custom attribute retrieval, method signature generation, type inspection, embedded resource access, and private member manipulation.
member.remarks:
This class extends various reflection types including , , , and to provide convenient helper methods for common reflection tasks. It also provides extensions for any object type through the Fuxion extensions framework to enable accessing private fields and properties for testing and advanced scenarios.
Key features include:
Custom attribute retrieval with error handling options
Human-readable method and type signature generation
Type hierarchy inspection and generic type definition matching
Embedded resource loading from assemblies
Private member access (fields and properties) for testing
Special handling for async methods and compiler-generated types

member.name: M:Fuxion.Reflection.ReflectionExtensions.AsyncMethodRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
<(?<method>.+?)>d__\\d+`*(?<num_args>\\d+)*
Explanation:
○ Match '<'.
○ "method" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' lazily at least once.
○ Match the string ">d__".
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Match '`' greedily any number of times.
○ Loop greedily and atomically any number of times.
○ "num_args" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.

member.name: M:Fuxion.Reflection.ReflectionExtensions.FileScopeClassNameRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(.*)<[a-zA-Z_]+>[A-F0-9]+__(.*)$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match '<'.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z_a-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match '>'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-F] atomically at least once.
○ Match the string "__".
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Fuxion.Response
member.summary: Represents the result of an operation with success/failure information and optional metadata.
member.param: Indicates whether the operation succeeded.
Optional message describing the result.
Optional error type categorization (e.g., ErrorType enum).
Optional exception that caused the failure.

remarks.para: This class implements the Result pattern (also known as Railway Oriented Programming) to provide a standardized way to handle operation outcomes without relying on exceptions for flow control.
Key benefits:

item.description: Explicit success/failure handling without exceptions
Rich metadata through Extensions dictionary
Type-safe error categorization
Implicit conversion to bool for easy checking
JSON serialization support with conditional properties

remarks.para: The Extensions dictionary allows attaching arbitrary metadata to responses, useful for:

item.description: HTTP status codes and headers
Validation errors
Correlation IDs
Performance metrics

member.name: M:Fuxion.Response.#ctor(System.Boolean,System.String,System.Object,System.Exception)
member.summary: Represents the result of an operation with success/failure information and optional metadata.
member.param: Indicates whether the operation succeeded.
Optional message describing the result.
Optional error type categorization (e.g., ErrorType enum).
Optional exception that caused the failure.

remarks.para: This class implements the Result pattern (also known as Railway Oriented Programming) to provide a standardized way to handle operation outcomes without relying on exceptions for flow control.
Key benefits:

item.description: Explicit success/failure handling without exceptions
Rich metadata through Extensions dictionary
Type-safe error categorization
Implicit conversion to bool for easy checking
JSON serialization support with conditional properties

remarks.para: The Extensions dictionary allows attaching arbitrary metadata to responses, useful for:

item.description: HTTP status codes and headers
Validation errors
Correlation IDs
Performance metrics

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.IsSuccess
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the operation was successful.
member.value: true if the operation succeeded; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.IsError
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the operation failed.
member.value: true if the operation failed; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This property is the inverse of and is provided for convenience. It is excluded from JSON serialization.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.Message
member.summary: Gets the message describing the result of the operation.
member.value: A message describing success or failure, or null if no message was provided.
member.remarks: This property is omitted from JSON when null.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.ErrorType
member.summary: Gets the error type categorization for failed operations.
member.value: An object representing the error type (typically an enum value), or null for successful operations.

remarks.para: This property is used to categorize errors for proper handling. Common error types include:

item.description: InvalidData - Client-side validation errors
NotFound - Resource not found
PermissionDenied - Authorization failures
Conflict - State conflicts
Critical - Unexpected server errors

remarks.para: This property is omitted from JSON when null.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.Exception
member.summary: Gets the exception that caused the operation to fail, if any.
member.value: The exception that occurred during the operation, or null if no exception occurred.

remarks.para: This property captures the original exception for logging and diagnostics while keeping the failure information in the Response object.
Uses a custom for JSON serialization to handle exception serialization safely (excluding non-serializable properties).
This property is omitted from JSON when default/null.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.Extensions
member.summary: Gets the dictionary of extension data for attaching arbitrary metadata to the response.
member.value: A dictionary with case-sensitive string keys containing additional response metadata.

remarks.para: This dictionary is serialized as JSON extension data (properties at the root level). It's commonly used for:

item.description: HTTP metadata (status codes, headers)
Validation error details
RFC 7807 Problem Details
Correlation/trace IDs
Performance metrics

member.name: M:Fuxion.Response.op_Implicit(Fuxion.Response)~System.Boolean
member.summary: Implicitly converts a Response to a boolean value.
member.param: The response to convert.
member.returns: true if the response indicates success; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This conversion allows using Response objects directly in conditional statements.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Response.Get
member.summary: Gets the Response factory methods for creating Response instances.
member.value: An instance providing access to static factory methods like Success(), Error(), etc.
member.remarks: This property provides a fluent API for creating Response objects through the ResponseExtensions class. Used as: Response.Get.Success(), Response.Get.Error(), etc.

member.name: T:Fuxion.Response`1
member.summary: Represents the result of an operation with a typed payload value.
member.typeparam: The type of the payload value.
member.param: Indicates whether the operation succeeded.
The payload value (required for success, typically null/default for failure).
Optional message describing the result.
Optional error type categorization.
Optional exception that caused the failure.

remarks.para: Extends to include a strongly-typed payload value. The payload is:

item.description: Required (non-null) when is true
Typically null/default when is false

remarks.para: The attributes ensure nullable reference type safety: When IsSuccess is true, the compiler knows Payload is not null.
Important restriction: Payload cannot be another Response type to prevent nested Response objects which would be confusing and violate the pattern's design.

member.name: T:Fuxion.ErrorType
member.summary: Defines standardized error categories for Response operations.

remarks.para: This enumeration provides semantic categorization of errors independent of transport protocols. These categories represent common error scenarios in business logic and application flows.
The error types can be mapped to various protocols:

item.description: HTTP status codes (see )
gRPC status codes
Custom error codes in your domain

remarks.para: The ensures that these values are serialized as strings in JSON (e.g., "NotFound" instead of 0), improving API clarity and version resilience.

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.NotFound
member.summary: The requested resource was not found.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: A resource with the specified identifier doesn't exist
An endpoint is valid but the resource is missing
A query returns no results when one was expected

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.PermissionDenied
member.summary: The request lacks valid authentication credentials or the authenticated user lacks necessary permissions.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Authentication is required but not provided or invalid
User is authenticated but lacks permission to access the resource
Token has expired or is invalid
Role-based access control denies the operation

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.InvalidData
member.summary: The request contains invalid or malformed data that fails validation.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Input validation fails (required fields, format, range)
Request payload is malformed or unparseable
Business rules validation fails
Data type mismatches or constraint violations

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.Conflict
member.summary: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource or with another concurrent operation.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Duplicate key or unique constraint violations
Optimistic concurrency conflicts (version mismatch)
State transition is not allowed
Resource dependencies prevent the operation

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.Critical
member.summary: An unexpected or critical error occurred on the server.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Unhandled exceptions occur
System-level errors prevent operation completion
Database connection failures
Configuration errors
Infinite loops or recursion detected

remarks.para: Important: Log these errors for diagnostics. Don't expose internal details to clients.

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.NotSupported
member.summary: The request uses an unsupported feature, protocol, or media type.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Unsupported Content-Type or media format
Feature not implemented in current version
Protocol upgrade required
Deprecated API version accessed

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.Unavailable
member.summary: The service is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance, overload, or external dependency failure.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Service is under maintenance
Server is overloaded
External dependency (database, API) is unavailable
Rate limiting is triggered
Circuit breaker is open

remarks.para: Consider including retry information in response extensions.

member.name: F:Fuxion.ErrorType.Timeout
member.summary: The request or an intermediate operation timed out.

remarks.para: Use when:

item.description: Client didn't send complete request in time
Server operation exceeded time limit
Upstream service didn't respond in time
Database query timeout

member.name: T:Fuxion.ResponseExtensions
member.summary: Provides extension methods and factory methods for creating and manipulating Response objects.

remarks.para: This class contains the complete API for working with Response objects, including:

item.description: Factory methods for creating success and error responses
Match pattern methods for functional-style response handling
Conversion methods between Response and Response<TPayload>
Typed error checking methods (IsNotFound, IsInvalidData, etc.)
Response combination methods for aggregating multiple results

member.name: T:Fuxion.ResponseExtensions.ResponseGetExtensions
member.summary: Factory methods for creating Response objects (accessed via Response.Get).

remarks.para: This class enables the fluent syntax: Response.Get.Success(), Response.Get.NotFound(), etc. All factory methods support optional extension data for attaching metadata to responses.
The class provides three categories of factory methods:

item.description: Success methods: Success(), SuccessMessage(), SuccessPayload()
Generic error methods: ErrorMessage(), ErrorPayload(), Exception()
Typed error methods: NotFound(), InvalidData(), PermissionDenied(), etc.

member.name: T:Fuxion.IResponse
member.summary: Defines the contract for a Response object representing the result of an operation.

remarks.para: This interface establishes the core structure of the Result pattern (Railway Oriented Programming) in Fuxion, providing a standardized way to handle operation outcomes without relying on exceptions for flow control.
The interface supports:

item.description: Success/failure state tracking
Descriptive error messages
Typed error categorization (ErrorType enum or custom types)
Exception capturing for diagnostics
Extensible metadata dictionary for arbitrary data
JSON serialization with custom converters

remarks.para: Implementation note: This interface uses to enable proper JSON serialization/deserialization of interface types to their concrete implementations.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.IsSuccess
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the operation was successful.
member.value: true if the operation succeeded; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This is the primary property for determining the outcome of an operation. When true, the operation completed successfully and any payload data (in IResponse<T>) is valid.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.IsError
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the operation failed.
member.value: true if the operation failed; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This is the inverse of and is provided for convenience and code readability. It is excluded from JSON serialization to avoid redundancy.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.Message
member.summary: Gets the message describing the result of the operation.
member.value: A human-readable message, or null if no message was provided.
member.remarks: This property should contain user-friendly text suitable for display in UIs or API responses. For success responses, it may describe what was accomplished. For error responses, it should explain what went wrong in clear, actionable terms without exposing sensitive system details. This property is omitted from JSON when null.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.ErrorType
member.summary: Gets the error type categorization for failed operations.
member.value: An object representing the error type (commonly an enum value), or null for successful operations or uncategorized errors.

remarks.para: This property enables semantic error handling by categorizing failures into standard types such as NotFound, InvalidData, PermissionDenied, etc. The type is intentionally defined as to allow flexibility:

item.description: Use the standard enum for common scenarios
Use custom enum types for domain-specific error categorization
Use string codes or other types if needed for specific use cases

remarks.para: When mapping to transport protocols (HTTP, gRPC, etc.), use extension methods in the appropriate namespace (e.g., for HTTP status code mapping).
This property is omitted from JSON when null.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.Exception
member.summary: Gets the exception that caused the operation to fail, if any.
member.value: The exception that occurred, or null if no exception was captured.

remarks.para: This property captures the original exception for logging, diagnostics, and debugging purposes while keeping the error information encapsulated in the Response object. This supports the Result pattern by avoiding exception-based flow control.
Uses for JSON serialization, which handles exception serialization safely by excluding non-serializable properties and capturing essential information like type, message, and stack trace.

Important: When exposing responses through APIs, ensure exception details are not leaked to end users in production environments. Log the full exception server-side but return sanitized messages to clients.
This property is omitted from JSON when null or default.

member.name: P:Fuxion.IResponse.Extensions
member.summary: Gets the dictionary of extension data for attaching arbitrary metadata to the response.
member.value: A dictionary with case-sensitive string keys containing additional response metadata. Never null - initialized to an empty dictionary if no extensions are provided.

remarks.para: This dictionary is serialized as JSON extension data using , meaning the key-value pairs are serialized as properties at the root level of the JSON object rather than nested under an "Extensions" property.
Common use cases for extensions include:

item.description: HTTP integration: status-code, reason-phrase, content-type, headers
RFC 7807 Problem Details: inner-problem, detail, instance, type
Validation errors: Field-level error details for InvalidData responses
Correlation/tracing: correlation-id, trace-id, span-id
Performance metrics: processing-time-ms, query-count, cache-hit
Pagination: page, page-size, total-count, has-next-page
Custom metadata: Any domain-specific data relevant to the response

remarks.para: Extension keys defined in : InnerProblemKey, JsonContentKey, JsonErrorKey, StringContentKey, PayloadKey, ExceptionKey, StatusCodeKey, ReasonPhraseKey, ContentLengthKey, ContentTypeKey, FileNameKey

member.name: T:Fuxion.SemanticVersion
member.summary: Represents a semantic version following the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification.

remarks.para: This class provides a complete implementation of Semantic Versioning (SemVer) as defined in the Semantic Versioning Specification.
Version format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILDMETADATA]

item.description: MAJOR: Incremented for incompatible API changes
MINOR: Incremented for backwards-compatible functionality additions
PATCH: Incremented for backwards-compatible bug fixes
PRERELEASE: Optional dot-separated identifiers (e.g., alpha.1, beta.2, rc.1)
BUILDMETADATA: Optional dot-separated identifiers for build information
Versions are compared by MAJOR, MINOR, and PATCH in order
Pre-release versions have lower precedence than normal versions (1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0)
Pre-release identifiers are compared lexicographically (numeric identifiers compared as integers)
Build metadata is ignored for precedence determination

remarks.para: The class uses the official SemVer regex from the specification (adapted for C# by removing 'P' prefixes from named groups). Framework compatibility: Uses GeneratedRegexAttribute on .NET 7+ for performance, falls back to traditional Regex on older frameworks.

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class from a version string.
member.param: A version string conforming to the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification. Format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILDMETADATA]
member.exception: Thrown when does not conform to the SemVer specification.

remarks.para: The version string is parsed using the official SemVer regex pattern. All components are validated:

item.description: MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH must be non-negative integers without leading zeros (except "0" itself)
PRERELEASE identifiers must contain only [0-9A-Za-z-] and cannot be empty between dots
BUILDMETADATA identifiers must contain only [0-9A-Za-z-] and cannot be empty between dots

member.name: P:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.Major
member.summary: Gets the major version number.
member.value: A non-negative integer representing incompatible API changes.

remarks.para: According to SemVer specification:

item.description: MUST be incremented if any backwards incompatible changes are introduced
MINOR and PATCH MUST be reset to 0 when MAJOR is incremented
MAJOR version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development; anything may change
Version 1.0.0 defines the public API

member.name: P:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.Minor
member.summary: Gets the minor version number.
member.value: A non-negative integer representing backwards-compatible functionality additions.

remarks.para: According to SemVer specification:

item.description: MUST be incremented if new, backwards-compatible functionality is introduced
MUST be incremented if any public API functionality is marked as deprecated
MAY be incremented if substantial new functionality or improvements are introduced within private code
PATCH MUST be reset to 0 when MINOR is incremented

member.name: P:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.Patch
member.summary: Gets the patch version number.
member.value: A non-negative integer representing backwards-compatible bug fixes.

remarks.para: According to SemVer specification:

item.description: MUST be incremented if only backwards-compatible bug fixes are introduced
A bug fix is defined as an internal change that fixes incorrect behavior

member.name: P:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.PreRelease
member.summary: Gets the pre-release version identifiers.
member.value: A collection of dot-separated identifiers, or empty if no pre-release version is specified.

remarks.para: Pre-release versions indicate that the version is unstable and might not satisfy the intended compatibility requirements.
Identifier rules:

item.description: MUST comprise only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens [0-9A-Za-z-]
MUST NOT be empty
Numeric identifiers MUST NOT include leading zeroes

remarks.para: Common pre-release identifiers: alpha, beta, rc (release candidate), followed by numeric versions (e.g., alpha.1, beta.2, rc.1).
Precedence: When comparing versions, pre-release versions have lower precedence than the associated normal version. Example: 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0

member.name: P:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.BuildMetadata
member.summary: Gets the build metadata identifiers.
member.value: A collection of dot-separated identifiers for build metadata, or empty if no build metadata is specified.

remarks.para: Build metadata MAY be denoted by appending a plus sign and a series of dot separated identifiers immediately following the patch or pre-release version.
Identifier rules:

item.description: MUST comprise only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens [0-9A-Za-z-]
MUST NOT be empty

remarks.para: Important: Build metadata SHOULD be ignored when determining version precedence. Thus, two versions that differ only in build metadata have the same precedence. Examples: 1.0.0+build.1 and 1.0.0+build.2 are considered equal for comparison purposes.
Common use cases: build numbers, commit SHA, timestamps (e.g., +20130313144700, +sha.5114f85, +build.123).

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Compares this instance with a specified object and returns an indication of their relative values.
member.param: An object to compare, or null.
member.returns: A signed integer that indicates the relative order: Less than zero if this instance precedes , zero if they have the same precedence, greater than zero if this instance follows or is null.
member.exception: Thrown when is not null and not a .

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.CompareTo(Fuxion.SemanticVersion)
member.summary: Compares this instance with another and returns an indication of their relative precedence.
member.param: A to compare with this instance, or null.
member.returns: A signed integer that indicates the relative precedence according to SemVer specification: Less than zero if this instance precedes , zero if they have the same precedence, greater than zero if this instance follows or is null.

remarks.para: Precedence is determined by the first difference when comparing:

item.description: MAJOR versions (higher is greater)
MINOR versions (higher is greater)
PATCH versions (higher is greater)
Pre-release versions (absence is greater than presence, then lexicographic comparison)

remarks.para: Build metadata is explicitly ignored during comparison per SemVer specification.

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.Equals(Fuxion.SemanticVersion)
member.summary: Determines whether this instance and another have the same value.
member.param: The to compare with this instance.
member.returns: true if the Major, Minor, Patch, and PreRelease components of are equal to this instance; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: Important: Build metadata is explicitly ignored during equality comparison per SemVer specification. Two versions differing only in build metadata are considered equal.
Example: 1.0.0+build.1 == 1.0.0+build.2 returns true.

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersion.SemanticVersionRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(?<major>0|[1-9]\\d*)\\.(?<minor>0|[1-9]\\d*)\\.(?<patch>0|[1-9]\\d*)(?:-(?<prerelease>(?:0|[1-9]\\d*|\\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*)(?:\\.(?:0|[1-9]\\d*|\\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*))*))?(?:\\+(?<buildmetadata>[0-9a-zA-Z-]+(?:\\.[0-9a-zA-Z-]+)*))?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ "major" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match '0'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically any number of times.
○ Match '.'.
○ "minor" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match '0'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically any number of times.
○ Match '.'.
○ "patch" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match '0'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily any number of times.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match '-'.
○ "prerelease" capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match '0'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily any number of times.

member.name: T:Fuxion.SemanticVersionException
member.summary: Represents errors that occur during semantic version parsing or validation.

remarks.para: This exception is thrown when a string cannot be parsed as a valid semantic version according to the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification. It inherits from to maintain consistency with Fuxion's exception hierarchy.
Common causes for this exception:

item.description: Invalid version format (e.g., missing components like "1.0" instead of "1.0.0")
Non-numeric major, minor, or patch components (e.g., "v1.0.0" with 'v' prefix)
Leading zeros in numeric components (e.g., "01.0.0" instead of "1.0.0")
Empty or invalid pre-release identifiers (e.g., "1.0.0-" with trailing hyphen)
Empty or invalid build metadata identifiers (e.g., "1.0.0+" with trailing plus)
Invalid characters in identifiers (only [0-9A-Za-z-] allowed)

remarks.para: Best practice: Use instead of the constructor when parsing user input or external data to avoid throwing exceptions for validation.

member.name: T:Fuxion.SemanticVersionIdentifier
member.summary: Represents a single identifier within a semantic version's pre-release or build metadata component.

remarks.para: According to the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification, pre-release versions and build metadata consist of dot-separated identifiers. This class represents one such identifier and implements the comparison rules defined in the SemVer specification.

item.description: Identifiers MUST comprise only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens [0-9A-Za-z-]
Identifiers MUST NOT be empty
Numeric identifiers MUST NOT include leading zeroes
Identifiers with only digits are compared numerically
Identifiers with letters or hyphens are compared lexically in ASCII sort order
Numeric identifiers always have lower precedence than non-numeric identifiers

remarks.para: Examples: 1 < 2 < 10 < alpha < beta (numeric comparison for numbers, then alphabetic)

member.name: M:Fuxion.SemanticVersionIdentifier.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The string value of the identifier. Must comply with SemVer rules: Only [0-9A-Za-z-] characters allowed, cannot be empty.

remarks.para: The constructor automatically determines if the identifier is purely numeric by attempting to parse it as a . This classification affects comparison behavior:

item.description: Numeric identifiers (e.g., "0", "1", "123") are compared numerically
Non-numeric identifiers (e.g., "alpha", "rc1", "build-123") are compared lexically

remarks.para: Note: This constructor does not validate that the identifier string conforms to SemVer rules. Validation is performed when parsing the full semantic version string.

member.name: T:Fuxion.SemanticVersionIdentifierCollection
member.summary: Represents a collection of semantic version identifiers used in pre-release or build metadata components.

remarks.para: According to the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification, pre-release versions and build metadata consist of dot-separated identifiers. This class represents such a collection and implements the comparison logic defined in the SemVer specification for identifier sequences.

item.description: A larger set of pre-release fields has higher precedence than a smaller set, if all preceding identifiers are equal
Identifiers are compared left-to-right until a difference is found
Each identifier is compared according to rules (numeric < alphanumeric)
1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 (shorter < longer when prefix matches)
1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-alpha.beta (numeric < alphanumeric)
1.0.0-alpha.beta < 1.0.0-beta (lexicographic comparison)
1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 (shorter < longer)
1.0.0-beta.2 < 1.0.0-beta.11 (numeric comparison: 2 < 11)
1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0-rc.1 (lexicographic: "beta" < "rc")

member.summary: Splits a string into individual words from various naming conventions. Handles camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, spaces, and acronyms.

remarks.para: This is a helper method used internally by case conversion methods (ToTitleCase, ToCamelCase, etc.). It intelligently handles various naming conventions and edge cases:

item.description: Separators: Splits on space, hyphen (-), and underscore (_)
camelCase/PascalCase: Splits when transitioning from lowercase to uppercase
Acronyms: Handles sequences like "XMLParser" → ["XML", "Parser"]
Mixed cases: "HTTPSConnection" → ["HTTPS", "Connection"]

remarks.para: Acronym detection logic: When encountering consecutive uppercase letters followed by a lowercase letter, the last uppercase letter is considered the start of a new word. For example: "XMLHttp" splits before 'H' → ["XML", "Http"].

example.code: // Internal usage examples (not directly accessible) SplitIntoWords("myVariableName") // yields: ["my", "Variable", "Name"] SplitIntoWords("MY_CONSTANT_NAME") // yields: ["MY", "CONSTANT", "NAME"] SplitIntoWords("kebab-case-string") // yields: ["kebab", "case", "string"] SplitIntoWords("XMLParser") // yields: ["XML", "Parser"] SplitIntoWords("HTTPSConnection") // yields: ["HTTPS", "Connection"] SplitIntoWords("IOError") // yields: ["IO", "Error"] SplitIntoWords("Hello World") // yields: ["Hello", "World"]

member.name: T:Fuxion.Text.Json.Serialization.SkipConverterFactory`1
member.summary: Provides a JSON converter factory that skips the execution of a wrapped converter for a specified number of invocations.
member.typeparam: The type of the JSON converter to wrap and control.
member.param: The converter instance to wrap and skip.
The number of times to skip the converter before allowing it to execute. Default is 1.

remarks.para: is a specialized wrapper that intercepts converter invocations and delays their execution until a specified skip count is reached. This is particularly useful for:

item.description: Preventing infinite recursion: When a custom converter needs to serialize/deserialize using default behavior
Conditional converter application: Applying a converter only after certain conditions are met
Converter chaining: Creating complex converter pipelines with controlled execution order
Debugging: Temporarily bypassing converters to isolate serialization issues
Performance optimization: Skipping expensive converters for specific scenarios

remarks.para: The factory maintains an internal counter that increments each time is called. When the counter reaches , the wrapped converter is allowed to execute:

item.description: Initial calls: Returns false from , incrementing the counter
After skip count: Delegates to the wrapped converter's logic
Converter creation: Creates the actual converter instance when needed

para.strong: Primary use case - Avoiding recursion in custom converters:

remarks.para: When implementing a custom that needs to call .Serialize or .Deserialize for the same type, you typically encounter infinite recursion because the serializer will invoke your converter again. solves this by temporarily removing your converter from the pipeline.

item.description: State management: The counter is instance-specific and not thread-safe by default
Skip count accuracy: Must match the exact number of recursion levels needed
Options cloning: The extension method creates new options to avoid mutating the original
Single converter assumption: The method expects exactly one instance of the target converter

remarks.para: If the wrapped converter is itself a , the skip factory correctly delegates both and calls to the underlying factory.

member.name: T:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile
member.summary: Defines a configuration profile that controls the concurrency behavior and execution patterns of tasks managed by .

remarks.para: is a struct that encapsulates various flags and settings to control how tasks are executed, queued, and managed. It provides predefined profiles for common scenarios and allows custom configuration through property combination.

item.description: Sequential execution: Tasks are queued and executed one after another, not concurrently
Cancellation: Previous tasks can be cancelled when new ones are queued
Last-only execution: Only the most recent task is executed, skipping queued ones
Instance-based: Concurrency control can be applied per instance rather than globally

remarks.para: The struct provides five static readonly profiles that cover common use cases:

item.description: : No special concurrency control (parallel execution)
: Execute tasks one at a time in order
: Sequential execution with cancellation of pending tasks
: Sequential execution but skip to the last queued task
: Combination of cancellation and last-only execution
Standard parallel task execution, no restrictions
Database transactions, file operations requiring order, state machines
UI updates where only the latest state matters, cancellable long-running operations
Search-as-you-type, live data filtering, throttled API calls
Real-time preview generation, aggressive throttling scenarios

remarks.para: You can create custom profiles by setting individual properties. For example, combining with other flags allows per-object concurrency control while sharing the same profile configuration.

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.Default
member.summary: Gets the default concurrency profile with no special restrictions, allowing parallel task execution.
member.value: A profile with all flags set to false.
member.remarks: This profile imposes no concurrency restrictions. Tasks created with this profile execute in parallel according to the .NET thread pool's default behavior. This is the standard behavior for most task scenarios.

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.RunSequentially
member.summary: Gets a profile that executes tasks sequentially, one at a time in the order they were queued.
member.value: A profile with set to true.

remarks.para: Tasks using this profile are queued and executed one after another. The next task doesn't start until the previous one completes. This ensures predictable ordering and prevents concurrent execution.

item.description: Order of execution matters (e.g., database transactions)
Resource access must be serialized (e.g., file operations)
State transitions must occur sequentially (e.g., state machines)

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.RunSequentiallyAndCancelPrevious
member.summary: Gets a profile that executes tasks sequentially and cancels any pending tasks when a new one is queued.
member.value: A profile with and set to true.

remarks.para: This profile combines sequential execution with aggressive cancellation. When a new task is queued, all pending (not yet started) tasks are cancelled, and only the new task executes after the current one completes.

item.description: Only the most recent operation matters (e.g., UI state updates)
Long-running operations should be cancelled if superseded
Resource cleanup is required when operations are abandoned

remarks.para: Note: Currently running tasks are NOT cancelled, only pending ones in the queue.

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.RunSequentiallyAndExecuteOnlyLast
member.summary: Gets a profile that executes tasks sequentially but skips intermediate tasks to execute only the last queued one.
member.value: A profile with and set to true.

remarks.para: This profile queues tasks sequentially but implements a "skip to latest" behavior. When multiple tasks are queued, only the most recently added task executes after the current one completes. Intermediate tasks are skipped entirely.

item.description: Rapid successive operations where intermediate results aren't needed (e.g., search-as-you-type)
Real-time data updates where only the latest value matters
Throttling without explicit delays (natural throttling through queue skipping)

remarks.para: Difference from : Tasks aren't cancelled but simply never started. This is useful when cancellation overhead isn't desired or when the task delegate doesn't support cancellation.

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.RunSequentiallyCancelPreviousAndExecuteOnlyLast
member.summary: Gets a profile that combines sequential execution, cancellation of previous tasks, and execution of only the last task.
member.value: A profile with , , and all set to true.

remarks.para: This is the most aggressive concurrency control profile. It combines:

item.description: Sequential execution (tasks run one at a time)
Cancellation of pending tasks
Skip-to-last behavior (only most recent task executes)
Maximum responsiveness to the latest request is critical
Resource cleanup via cancellation is important
Intermediate operations are completely unnecessary
Heavy throttling with cancellation support is needed

remarks.para: Example scenarios: Real-time preview generation where generating previews for intermediate states is wasteful, or live search with expensive backend queries that should be cancelled if superseded.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional name for the concurrency profile for debugging and identification purposes.
member.value: A string identifying the profile, or null if not set.
member.remarks: This property is purely for documentation and debugging. It doesn't affect the profile's behavior but can be useful when logging, profiling, or diagnosing concurrency issues.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.ByInstance
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether concurrency control should be applied per instance rather than globally.
member.value: true if concurrency control is instance-specific; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: When true, the concurrency profile's restrictions (sequencing, cancellation, etc.) apply independently to each instance or context that uses the profile. When false, restrictions apply globally across all tasks using the same profile.
Note: The exact behavior of this flag depends on the implementation and how it tracks and groups task instances.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.Sequentially
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether tasks should be executed sequentially rather than in parallel.
member.value: true if tasks should execute one at a time; otherwise, false for parallel execution.

remarks.para: When true, tasks are queued and executed in FIFO (First-In-First-Out) order. The next task waits until the previous task completes before starting.
This is the foundation flag for all sequential execution profiles. It's typically combined with other flags like or to achieve specific behaviors.
Performance consideration: Sequential execution may reduce throughput compared to parallel execution but ensures predictable ordering and can simplify reasoning about task dependencies and state.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.ExecuteOnlyLast
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether only the last queued task should be executed, skipping intermediate tasks.
member.value: true to execute only the most recent task; otherwise, false to execute all queued tasks.

remarks.para: When true and combined with , the task queue implements a "skip-to-latest" behavior. As tasks are queued, intermediate tasks are marked to be skipped, and only the most recently added task will execute once the current task completes.
Typical usage: Search-as-you-type, live filtering, auto-save debouncing, real-time calculations where only the final result matters.
Important: This flag typically requires to be true to be meaningful. Without sequential execution, there's no queue from which to skip tasks.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ConcurrencyProfile.CancelPrevious
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether pending tasks should be cancelled when a new task is queued.
member.value: true to cancel pending tasks when new ones arrive; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: When true, any tasks that are queued but not yet started are cancelled when a new task is added to the queue. This is useful for scenarios where only the most recent operation is relevant and older operations can be safely abandoned.

item.description: Cancelled: Tasks that are queued but haven't started executing yet
NOT cancelled: The currently executing task (it runs to completion or until it checks cancellation tokens)

remarks.para: Use with caution: Ensure your task delegates properly handle cancellation if they allocate resources or perform operations that need cleanup. Use parameters in your task delegates for proper cancellation support.

item.description: : Tasks are actively cancelled (cancellation tokens are triggered)
: Tasks are simply skipped without cancellation notification

member.name: T:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledByConcurrencyException
member.summary: Represents an exception that is thrown when a task is canceled due to concurrency control mechanisms.
member.remarks:
This exception is a specialized version of used to indicate that a task was canceled specifically because of concurrency management logic, rather than a general cancellation request. This distinction allows for more precise exception handling and debugging in scenarios where concurrent task execution needs to be controlled or limited.
Common scenarios where this exception might be thrown include:
Rate limiting or throttling mechanisms that prevent too many concurrent operations
Resource pool exhaustion where only a limited number of concurrent tasks are allowed
Mutex or semaphore-based concurrency control that cancels tasks when access is denied
Task deduplication where duplicate concurrent operations are canceled

member.name: T:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.TaskManager
member.summary: Provides advanced task management capabilities with tracking, concurrency control, and enhanced creation options.

remarks.para: is a static utility class that extends the standard functionality by providing:

item.description: Task Tracking: All tasks created through TaskManager are tracked and can be queried
Concurrency Profiles: Built-in concurrency control through
Current Task Access: Easy access to the currently executing managed task via
Overload Support: Methods for 0-9 parameters with both synchronous and asynchronous delegates
Return Value Support: Both void and result-returning task creation
Thread-Safe Operations: All internal task tracking is thread-safe via

remarks.para: The class is implemented as a partial class split across three files:

item.description: TaskManager.cs: Core infrastructure, task storage, and entry management
TaskManager2.cs: Void-returning task creation methods (Action delegates)
TaskManager3.cs: Result-returning task creation methods (Func delegates)
Automatic task tracking and lifecycle management
Concurrency profile support for controlling execution patterns
Access to task metadata through
Automatic cleanup when tasks complete

member.name: F:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.TaskManager.Tasks
member.summary: Thread-safe storage for all managed tasks with their associated metadata.

remarks.para: This locker protects a list of instances, where each entry contains:

item.description: The actual instance
Metadata about task creation (scheduler, options, concurrency profile)

remarks.para: Entries are automatically added when tasks are created and removed when tasks complete. All access to this collection is synchronized through the wrapper.

member.name: P:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.TaskManager.Current
member.summary: Gets the current managed task, if the calling code is executing within a task created by .
member.value:
The instance of the currently executing managed task, or null if:
The current code is not executing within a TaskManager-created task
The task was not created through TaskManager
is null

remarks.para: This property uses to identify the calling task and looks it up in the managed task collection. This is useful for:

item.description: Accessing task metadata from within task execution
Debugging and logging task information
Implementing task-local storage patterns

remarks.para: Performance note: This property performs a thread-safe search through the managed task list on each access. Consider caching the result if accessed frequently within a task.

member.name: M:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.TaskManager.AddEntry(Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.ITaskManagerEntry)
member.summary: Adds a task entry to the managed task collection and sets up automatic cleanup on completion.
member.param: The task entry to add to the tracking system.

remarks.para: This method performs two key operations:

item.description: Registers a continuation on the task that will automatically remove the entry from the collection when the task completes (regardless of outcome: success, fault, or cancellation).
Adds the entry to the thread-safe collection for tracking.

remarks.para: Automatic Cleanup: The continuation ensures that completed tasks don't accumulate in memory. The cleanup happens asynchronously after task completion.
Thread Safety: Both the continuation registration and the collection modification are thread-safe operations.

member.name: T:Fuxion.Threading.Tasks.Extensions
member.summary: Provides extension methods for and of to enhance task management capabilities with cancellation, continuation, and sleep functionality.

remarks.para: This static class uses C# 14.0 extension syntax to add methods directly to and task collection types. The extensions integrate tightly with to provide advanced task control features not available in standard TPL (Task Parallel Library).

item.description: Cancellation control: Cancel, check cancellation state, and access cancellation tokens
Fluent continuations: OnCancel, OnSuccess, OnFaulted methods for cleaner continuation syntax
Cancellable sleep: Task.Delay alternative that respects task cancellation
Batch operations: Cancel and wait for multiple tasks simultaneously

remarks.para: Most methods require tasks to be created through rather than standard Task.Run or Task.Factory. This is because TaskManager maintains additional metadata (cancellation tokens, entry tracking) that these extensions rely on.
Important: Unless otherwise noted, these extension methods only work with tasks created by . Using them with standard TPL tasks may throw exceptions or return default values.

member.name: T:Fuxion.IUndefinable`1
member.summary: Defines the contract for types that can represent undefined values.
member.typeparam: The type of the value when defined.
member.remarks:
This interface enables distinguishing between three states:
undefined: The value has not been set or provided
null: The value has been explicitly set to null
defined: The value has been set to a non-null value
This distinction is particularly useful in scenarios like JSON PATCH operations, GraphQL mutations, or API updates where you need to differentiate between "don't change this field" (undefined), "set this field to null" (null), and "set this field to this value" (defined).

member.name: T:Fuxion.Undefinable`1
member.summary: Represents a value that can be in one of three states: undefined, null, or defined with a value.
member.typeparam: The type of the value when defined.

remarks.para: is a readonly struct that enables distinguishing between:

item.description: Undefined: The value has not been provided or set (useful for optional fields in updates)
Null: The value has been explicitly set to null (clear/delete the field)
Defined: The value has been set to a specific value (update the field)
Undefined: Serialized as [null] (array with single null element)
Null: Serialized as null
Defined: Serialized as the value itself

remarks.para: The special [null] format for undefined values is used because JSON doesn't have a native "undefined" type, and this format is distinguishable from both null and actual array values.

item.description: JSON PATCH operations where you need to know which fields to update
GraphQL mutations where undefined means "don't change"
REST API updates where you want to distinguish between "no value provided" and "explicitly null"
Configuration systems where undefined uses a default but null disables a feature

item.description: Selective deserialization: Only properties present in JSON are added to the Patcher's internal dictionary
Property tracking: Maintains a mapping of property names to their (PropertyInfo, value) tuples
Type-safe serialization: Preserves property types during round-trip serialization
Private constructor support: Uses for types with non-public constructors
Null handling: Distinguishes between "property not provided" and "property set to null"

Reads the JSON object token by token using

For each property in the JSON:
Gets the property name from the JSON token
Resolves the corresponding using reflection
Deserializes the property value using and .Deserialize
Adds the (PropertyInfo, value) pair to the Patcher's internal dictionary
Returns the populated instance
Writes a JSON start object token
Iterates through all properties in the Patcher's internal dictionary

For each property:
Writes the property name
Serializes the property value using the Fuxion JSON extension methods
Writes the raw JSON value
Writes a JSON end object token

remarks.para: The converter includes robust error handling with descriptive exceptions:

item.description: - When Patcher instance creation fails, property name can't be read, or property doesn't exist on type T
- When unexpected JSON tokens are encountered or serialization fails

remarks.para: Type constraint: The generic parameter is constrained to class (reference types) because the Patcher pattern is designed for mutable reference types typically used in DTOs and domain models.

remarks.para: is a specialized that dynamically creates instances of for any closed generic type derived from . This enables automatic JSON conversion support for the Patcher pattern, which is commonly used in HTTP PATCH operations to track and apply partial updates to objects.

The Patcher pattern allows for selective property updates where only the properties explicitly set in the JSON payload are updated, leaving other properties unchanged. This is particularly useful for:

item.description: RESTful APIs: Implementing HTTP PATCH endpoints that update only specified fields
Partial updates: Distinguishing between "not provided" and "set to null" in API requests
Form submissions: Processing incomplete or partial form data
Delta tracking: Recording which properties have been modified

Returns the converter instance to be used by the JSON serialization infrastructure

remarks.para: The factory performs runtime type validation to ensure the converter is created correctly. If fails to create the converter instance, an is thrown with a descriptive message.
To enable Patcher support, add this factory to the converters collection in your . Once registered, all types will be automatically handled during JSON operations.
